briefs.caption:
A pro club wants to put $350K into college fields ⚽🏟️

Fort Lauderdale United FC and Broward College announced a proposal for an estimated $350,000 in upgrades at Broward College's Central Campus: baseball fields converted into multipurpose soccer fields, new grass, upgraded irrigation and restored field lighting.

Broward College students and intramurals get first priority. FTL UTD would get space for youth development, clinics, training and community events.

Our take: more lit, soccer-ready fields means more room for youth programs and pickup in Broward. It's still a proposal, so we'll be watching for construction dates.

briefs.caption:
Your kid's age group changed this season. Here's why. 👇

For 2026-27, US Youth Soccer, US Club Soccer and AYSO moved youth soccer from birth-year to school-year age groups: August 1 to July 31 instead of January to December.

Example: U-12 is now born Aug 1, 2014 to Jul 31, 2015. Born August to December? Your player likely moves to a younger age group than under the old rule. Born January to July? Same group as before.

Leagues could choose their system, so confirm your league's chart and ask clubs which age group your player tries out for.

briefs.caption:
Messi did it again. First ever. ⚽👟

Lionel Messi won the 2026 MLS Golden Boot with 26 goals, the league's top scorer for the second straight season. He is the first player in MLS history to win back-to-back Golden Boots. FC Dallas' Petar Musa (22) and Nashville SC's Sam Surridge (21) finished behind him.

He added 17 assists for a league-best 43 goal contributions.

Our take: at this level, the assists matter as much as the goals. Next up: playoff Game 1 vs Columbus Crew, Saturday Nov 21 at Nu Stadium.

briefs.caption:
Beckham paid $25 million. San Diego paid a reported $500M. 💰

When David Beckham joined LA Galaxy in 2007, his contract included an option to buy an MLS expansion team for $25 million. He used it in 2014, and Inter Miami started playing in 2020.

The price of getting in has changed: Charlotte FC's fee was reported near $325 million, and San Diego FC, awarded in May 2023, paid a reported $500 million.

Our take: MLS has no promotion or relegation, so a team can't play its way in. The seat itself is the asset, and Forbes valued Inter Miami at about $1.2 billion in 2025.

Source: Wikipedia (Inter Miami CF, San Diego FC, Charlotte FC), citing Forbes and media reports.
